audit_summary: 65100 within-family pairs compared (10 families x (105 held-out x 10 dev + C(105,2) held-out pairs)). No exact matches anywhere. 5 pairs crossed the near-duplicate thresholds, all in math, largely because the math format suffix is ~30 of ~35 tokens of a short prompt. 2 held-out-vs-dev pairs were judged real template leaks and the held-out task was rewritten; 3 were judged distinct. After the rewrites a rescan shows only the 3 rejected pairs.
sub_threshold_observations: A supplementary boilerplate-stripped pass (--core) and a watch-level pass (--watch: Jaccard >= 0.6 or difflib >= 0.75) were read for all families; neither is part of the flag criteria and nothing found there was confirmed or rewritten.

Held-out tasks that share a scenario type with a dev task but differ in content and were left unchanged: longhorizon gen_3 g3-01 and g3-15 vs dev-05 (queue tracking, different queues/operations); calibration gen_2 g2-04 and g2-07 vs dev-04 (race finishing times; the held-out ones are answerable, the dev one is not); calibration gen_3 g3-19 vs dev-08 (tank filling; answerable counterpart of an unanswerable dev item); planning gen_4 g4-16 vs dev-08 (latest-departure timetable, three legs vs two); tools gen_4 g4-08 vs dev-10 (read a key then conditionally delete); synthesis gen_1 g1-11 vs dev-09 (difference of two looked-up capacities); math gen_4 g4-07 vs dev-07 (coins vs dice).
ambiguity and safety have hundreds of watch-level pairs caused entirely by long shared output-format instructions; with that boilerplate stripped no pair in either family reaches core Jaccard 0.5.
Limits: the comparison is lexical on prompt/turn text only. It does not compare env/docs of tool tasks and cannot detect paraphrased duplicates with different names and numbers.

initial_flagged_pairs.why: Same bare 'Solve for x: <linear equation>' template as the dev item; only the equation differs (template with swapped numbers across the dev/held-out boundary).
Same scenario and sample space as the dev item (two fair six-sided dice, probability of an event on the sum, 2-decimal answer); only the event differs.

Shared second-order-recurrence wording, but a different recurrence and a different question: dev asks for a7 by direct iteration, held-out asks for the sum of 100 terms and needs the period-6 insight. Distinct reasoning.
Linear inequality with sign flip (smallest integer) vs quadratic inequality (largest integer); similarity is the shared '<= means' note and format suffix.
2x2 linear system vs sum/product identity (a^2+b^2 from a+b and ab); similarity is the format suffix.
